A1.justification: Both PDFs contain complete, readable versions of the same MOOSE-Chem work. The main text, 20 tables, two figures, and appendices can be matched, including the reordered overview and proof sections.

before.justification: v5 reports original retrieval, hypothesis-generation, ranking, baseline, ablation, and expert-evaluation results on its 51-paper benchmark, including supplementary analyses and case studies.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Sections 5–6 and the appendices. Retained results include automatic and expert evaluations.

M1.justification: Retrieval, evolutionary mutation/refinement/recombination, hypothesis scoring, and beam search remain unchanged. The explicit Markov Decision Process formulation describes the existing procedure without introducing a new training or inference component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 51 chemistry/materials papers, inspiration corpora of 150–3,000 papers, and retrieval, generation, and ranking tasks. Oracle-inspiration, copilot, and background-survey scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 5, 10, 13, and 14 retain the same Llama/GPT-4o comparisons and SciMON, MOOSE, and Qi et al. baselines. The shortened SciMON description does not establish a changed comparator implementation.

E3.justification: Model settings, corpus construction, screening procedures, evaluation metrics, and expert-selection procedures remain unchanged. Both versions select the top two hypotheses for the oracle-inspiration expert evaluation and the top four for the copilot evaluation.

E4.justification: The same screening-window, multi-step, evolutionary-unit, significance-feedback, and background ablations remain. Alternative-judge evaluations, ranking analyses, agreement analyses, and all four appendix case studies are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Expert-agreement sampling and hard/soft consistency definitions in Appendices A.14–A.15 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 20 tables retain identical entries, and the case-study findings are unchanged. For example, Table 10 still reports MOOSE-Chem Top/Average Matched Scores of 4.020/2.564 and SciMON scores of 2.549/2.281.

T1.justification: Former Appendix A.1, now A.2, adds a unique minimal inspiration-set assumption. v6 Equations 5–8 replace the initial direct joint-probability equality with marginalization followed by uniqueness and fixed-order reductions; the fixed-order assumption already existed later in v5. An explicit MDP state/action/transition/reward formulation and revised derivation explanations substantially change the foundations of the central proof, although its final factorization is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims about three-component decomposition, the 51-paper benchmark, rediscovery of unseen chemistry hypotheses, and latent scientific knowledge associations.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.2 extend the existing Markov interpretation into an explicit policy-and-reward account aimed at maximizing expected final hypothesis quality. Existing interpretations and caveats concerning Matched Score, ranking reliability, and expert evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v6 adds a first-page repository link described as providing all code and data; v5 has no corresponding access pointer. Section 6.1 also removes the explicit statement that SciMON shares MOOSE-Chem's retriever, reducing documentation detail without demonstrating an implementation change.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussions retain the same works and substantive positioning, including comparisons with literature-based discovery, reasoning, retrieval, and self-consistency. No revised novelty claim or substantive repositioning is established.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the expanded proof explanations, swapping the overview and proof appendices, shortening the SciMON paragraph, and small contact-information and wording changes. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 18 to page 15, loses the optional-survey and chemistry qualifiers in its labels, and receives expanded accompanying explanation. Several tables move within or across pages, while their structures and contents remain unchanged; Figure 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v5's direct probability equality, v6 makes the marginalization and assumptions supporting its reduction explicit, improving the derivation's transparency. The new code/data pointer also improves reproducibility documentation. These are limited net gains despite some lost SciMON detail; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
